sources.entry: Files Sharing - File sharing application based on unique and temporary links. GPL-3.0 PHP/Docker

summary.one_liner: A self-hosted PHP/Laravel web app for sharing files through unique, temporary bundle links, similar to WeTransfer, with no database required.
summary.what_it_does: Lets an uploader gather one or more files into a bundle by drag and drop or file browsing, then set a title, description, expiration date, maximum number of downloads and optional password. Each bundle yields two links, a preview link that shows the contents and allows a ZIP download, and a direct download link that skips the preview; both use the same authorization code. Uploads can be restricted by IP address (single, wildcard, CIDR or range) or by login and password, and both can be combined. A scheduled Artisan command removes expired bundle files from storage every five minutes, and a manual purge command is also available. The README says it stores data in JSON files rather than a database, and includes a download rate limiter and English, French, German and Korean translations.
use_cases: Sending large files to clients or colleagues without email attachments
Running a private WeTransfer-style service on your own server
Sharing files through links that expire automatically
Letting external recipients download a bundle as one ZIP
Collecting uploads from people on a trusted IP range or with login accounts
how_to_run: docker run -d -p 8080:80 -v :/app/storage/content --name filesharing -e APP_NAME="FileSharing" axeloz/filesharing:latest (the README example also sets APP_URL, ASSET_URL, upload and rate limit variables)
Standalone: clone the repo into the webroot and point the web server at ./public
Run composer install, then yarn --production (or npm install --production), then yarn build (or npm run build)
Make ./storage writable by PHP, run php artisan key:generate, and copy .env.example to .env to edit it
Optionally create a user with php artisan fs:user:create
Add the Laravel scheduler to cron: * * * * * /usr/bin/php /path-to-your-project/artisan schedule:run
notable: No database server needed; data is kept as JSON files in the storage folder
Two links per bundle: a preview page and a direct download link, both gated by one authorization code
Expired bundles are removed automatically by a scheduled Laravel Artisan command every five minutes
Upload access can be limited by IP range (CIDR, wildcard, start-end) or login, or both
Ships with a Docker image and environment variables for upload size, file count, duplicate checks and download rate
caveats: Uploads are publicly accessible if UPLOAD_LIMIT_IPS is left empty and no users are created, per the README warning
Large uploads through Nginx need client_max_body_size raised, and PHP upload and memory limits must be set to match UPLOAD_MAX_FILESIZE
Standalone install needs cron access to run the scheduler for bundle deletion
Roadmap items such as unit tests, asynchronous ZIP creation and white labeling are not yet implemented
